subcategory: education regulation — private schools, home schooling
name: Québec — private educational institutions and home schooling
name_fr: Québec — établissements d'enseignement privés et enseignement à la maison
description: Québec private schools hold a permit from the Ministère de l'Éducation under the Act respecting private education; some are also accredited for subsidies (agréés aux fins de subventions). All must meet ministerial requirements for programs of study and pedagogical supervision; each sets its own admission rules. Home schooling requires an annual notice to the Ministry's Direction de l'enseignement à la maison by 1 July, a learning project implemented by 30 September, monitoring and an end-of-year report (by 15 June), and evaluation by one of the regulated methods.

attributes.legal_term: Établissement d'enseignement privé (Act respecting private education, CQLR c. E-9.1)
attributes.categories: Permit holder; subsidised (agréé aux fins de subventions) or unsubsidised. A sector body (FEEP, 2024–2025 briefs) states no new subsidy accreditations have been granted since 2008 — not confirmed by the ministry.
attributes.curriculum: Must conform to ministerial requirements on programs of study and pedagogical supervision (Québec Education Program); secondary studies lead to the DES.
attributes.register: Ministry open-data layer 'Installation d'enseignement privé' lists 353 private installations with language(s) of instruction (updated 2026-10-26); it does not show subsidy status.
attributes.language: See nat-qc-education-english-instruction-eligibility. Instruction in subsidised private schools follows the Charter of the French Language; unsubsidised schools may teach in English but time spent there does not create eligibility.
attributes.home_schooling: Regulation respecting home schooling (CQLR c. I-13.3, r. 6.01, in force 1 July 2018): notice by 1 July (or within 10 days of leaving school); learning project by 30 September; follow-up with the ministry; evaluation through a school service centre/board, a private institution, a licensed teacher, a portfolio, or a ministerial exam; school service centres provide support on request.
attributes.funding: Subsidised private schools receive ministry funding under the budget rules; unsubsidised receive none.
